fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. In verse 30, God says, “…I have given every green plant for food.” He says it about every beast of the earth, every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth. So He provides for them, and leaving them to find food on their own doesn't match the verse.

Yes, friend! In verse 3, God said, “Let there be light…” and there was light. He said it, and there it was. It's the first time God speaks in the story, and I think that's a pretty strong way to start talking.

Not quite, friend. In verse 22, God blesses them and tells the sea creatures to be fruitful, multiply and fill the waters, and the birds to multiply on the earth. Nothing in the blessing tells them to stay put. I stayed put in a drawer for years, and I can tell you it wasn't my favorite way to spend a decade.

That's right, friend. In verse 26, God says man is to “…rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air…” and over the livestock and the earth too. The list goes from the sea to the sky to the ground. That's a lot of territory to be handed, and I get nervous just managing one bakery.

problems.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.
Calling light the first thing on the list overlooks the heavens and the earth, which God created in verse 1.
The explanation says God told both the sea creatures and the birds to fill the waters. He told the sea creatures to fill the waters and the birds to multiply on the earth.
The joke imagines a blessing saying “don't move” in the context of God's blessing. Jokes must not put invented words in God's mouth.
“Nothing gets left out” goes beyond the things God names as being under man's rule.
